answer:
Based on my research of the Metropolitan Museum of Art's collection database for Edwin Austin Abbey holiday cards, I found that the Met holds **two holiday/Christmas cards** by Edwin Austin Abbey in its Open Access program:

1. **Object Number 64.636.4** - "Man Delivering a Holiday Box" (1906)
   - According to the Signatures, Inscriptions, and Markings section: *"Abbey drew this Christmas card and used it to send greetings, to an unnamed recipient, from himself and his wife in 1906."*

2. **Object Number 64.636.1** - "Man Walking in the Snow Carrying a Covered Basket, Accompanied by a Small Terrier" (1890–1911)
   - According to the Signatures, Inscriptions, and Markings section: *"Abbey drew this holiday card and used it to send greetings to an unknown recipient from himself and his wife."*

**Answer:** There are **no** Edwin Austin Abbey holiday cards in the Metropolitan Museum of Art's Open Access collection that are explicitly addressed to a specific person by name or initials. Both holiday cards documented in the Met's collection were sent to **"unnamed"** or **"unknown"** recipients, as clearly stated in each artwork's Signatures, Inscriptions, and Markings section. The cards do not contain dedicated inscriptions with specific names or initials of intended recipients.

**Beatles Autographed Postcard With Jimmie Nichol Signature, 1964.** John, Paul, George, and...Jimmie? On the day before the start of the Beatles' 1964 tour of Europe and the Far East, Ringo suddenly came down with tonsillitis and was admitted to a London hospital. With little time to spare, Brian Epstein enlisted George Martin to help find a replacement. Martin had the ideal candidate, a talented young drummer named Jimmie Nichol, whom he knew from a recent Tommy Quickly session. Nichol duly had one practice session with the the other three, and 27 hours later was taking the stage with them for the first tour date in Copenhagen on June 4. After his surgery and recuperation, Ringo rejoined the others onstage on June 15 in Australia, and Nichol's 11 days in the most famous pop group in history came to an end. Jimmie was apparently the first to sign this BOAC postcard of London, writing "To Lynne, Best Wishes, Jimmie Nichol" followed by Paul, John, and George, all in bold black ink. In overall Very Good condition, some creases and an apparent fold at center, and two sets of staple holes in one corner. _COA from Frank Caiazzo._
**Beatles Group Autographed Photo Including Both Ringo Starr and Pete Best Signatures.** This vintage photograph of the Beatles was taken in late 1961, when the group was still sporting the black leather look adopted in Hamburg and Pete Best was still the drummer. The back of the photo was signed in late 1962 by the group, however, after Best had been replaced by Ringo Starr. John, Paul, George, and Ringo have all signed boldly in black ink, with John and Paul adding "Love", and all four adding "XXX," which was common in the early days. Pete Best's signature was added later in blue ink, making this a truly rare collection of Beatle autographs. In Very Good condition, with some slight edge wear and several small stains, and several small scratches to the frame. The piece has been nicely matted with a Ringo-lineup custom matte to the front, and a cutaway to the back allowing viewing of the Best-lineup photo. _COA from Tracks, LTD._

Beatles Autographed _Beatles For Sale_ Albums Here is a fantastic presentation piece which is a terrifically clever display of the Beatles' fourth album _Beatles For Sale._ Within the framed display are two separate copies of the LP which together contain a full set of signatures of all four of the Beatles, and allows for enjoyment of both sides of the album artwork. To the left on the color cover photograph by Robert Freeman are bold black signatures rendered in felt tip by John, Ringo, and Paul, just above their respective images. To the right, George has written "Best Wishes from George Harrison" in black ballpoint next to his image of the group in performance at their first US concert at the Washington Coliseum. The overall impact of the two covers together is quite stunning, and is simply one of the best displays of Beatle signatures we've ever seen. Also presented is side one of the LP, all three elements matted within a black composite frame measuring approximately 34" x 34". _COA from Frank Caiazzo, dating both signature pieces to early 1965._
**Beatles Set Of Autographs, 1963.**
Here is as beautiful and as straightforward a set of early Beatles autographs as one could hope for. Signed on a light blue page taken from an autograph book are all four signatures in bold blue ink. Ringo has added "The Beatles" just above his signature at top, and added his "star" line below. The autograph sheet measures approximately 4" x 6" and is in Excellent condition. It is presented beneath a very sharp 10.5" x 13" photograph of the Beatles performing for television in 1963, both professionally matted and in a black wooden frame measuring 21.5" x 19". _COA from Perry Cox._

**Beatles Autographs On British Governmental Stationery, Early 1960s.** This fine set of Beatles autographs dates to the early 1960s, and were purportedly obtained by a British air transit officer when the group returned to the UK from an overseas tour. That would seem quite plausible, as the signatures are affixed to a piece of ruled paper which bears the crest of the British government. The sheet is 12.75" x 8" overall, and had likely been folded in half, lengthwise, when presented to the Beatles for signing, as the autographs are neatly centered on the right half of the page. Paul has signed at top in bold blue ink, and the other three have added their autographs in black ink. The paper is in Very Good condition, with some yellowing from age and folded lengthwise as mentioned, and with an additional horizontal and vertical fold. There is an approximate 1" tear through the horizontal fold, front and back, which does go through the crest but does not impact the autographs._COA From Heritage Auctions._
**Beatles: Signatures of John, Paul, and Ringo on a Postcard Obtained During the****_Magical Mystery Tour_****Filming, with Four Color Snapshots.** A 6" x 4" color glossy postcard of "Watergate Bay, near Newquay, Cornwall" signed on the message side by three in ink: "_To Anne love from John Lennon_", "_Paul McCartney_", and "_Ringo Starr_". The Beatles and their tour bus pulled up at the Atlantic Hotel in Newquay on the evening of September 12, 1967, intending to stay one night. They ended up spending three nights at the hotel and filmed various scenes in the area. These autographs were obtained at the hotel, possibly on the 13th when George was unavailable for filming while he was giving an extensive interview to the BBC. Beatle autographs from 1967 are much rarer than earlier examples. The signatures are a bit light but clear and legible, overall Fine condition. _COA from Tracks LTD._
Also included are four 3.5" square color candid snapshots, one of each Beatle, taken at the same hotel during the above-mentioned dates. Excellent.

**Beatles Fully Autographed Cavern Club Booklet, Including Both Ringo Starr and Pete Best** This vintage 1963 Season Cavern Club membership booklet and additional pages from a similar 1961 booklet gave the young fan who owned it the rare distinction of having signatures by five members of the Beatles, namely John, Paul, George, Ringo, and the group's original drummer, Pete Best.
The signatures are featured on several pages within the booklet and on pages from a 1961 version of the booklet, and were obtained by a young fan in Liverpool named Sheila Stewart. One signed page bears the inscriptions "To Sheila love from John Lennon X" and "To Sheila love from Paul McCartney XXX" in blue ink. Another bears signatures in red ink from McCartney, Starr, Best, and Gerry Marsden of Gerry & The Pacemakers, with Starr adding "The Sensational" and "DRUM" to his autograph. George Harrison signed on the following page in red ballpoint, and Best inscribed "Lots of Love to Sheila Pete Best XXX" in red ink.
A great collection of Beatles signatures, signed while on the cusp of celebrity. Signed Cavern Club membership books are very rare, and few signed by the Beatles are known to exist. The presence of Best's signature makes this even more desirable.
The booklet measures approximately 4.5" x 2" when closed, and exhibits expected wear. In overall Very Good condition, with some slight edgewear, creases, and small stains. _LOA from Frank Caiazzo._

**Beatles (as Tony Sheridan and The Beat Brothers) "My Bonnie/ The Saints" Promo 45 (Decca 31382, 1962).** One of the most important vinyl discs ever produced is this innocuous pink label promo recording on the familiar Decca label. It was all but ignored in the US where this was released, as were the Beatles in general in 1962. The Fab were beginning to make a name for themselves in their Liverpool hometown and garnering a following in the unlikely locale of Hamburg, Germany, where they worked alongside fellow Brit, Tony Sheridan. When Polydor signed Sheridan, the label selected the Beatles to back him on a single, calling the group "The Beat Brothers" to avoid tricky translation problems. The two Tin Pan Alley standards that were recorded were released to some success -- but only in Germany. Decca, an American affiliate of Polydor, issued pink label promo copies and black label commercial copies in the States to absolutely no avail! America wasn't ready for the British Invasion in 1962! It would be two years later in 1964, after the launch of Beatlemania in the US, that MGM would reissue this single, and only then did the record, now credited solely to The Beatles, enjoy commercial success. The Decca version is the very first American release by the Beatles, whose name doesn't even appear on the label! Rare without question, and in this condition practically unique. Condition: MT 9.
**Beatles ("Beattles") "Please Please Me/ Ask My Why" Rare Promo 45 (Vee-Jay 498, 1963).** The second rarest Vee-Jay promo single comes in two versions: one with the group's name spelled correctly, another - as offered here - with the Fab's name misspelled "Beattles". You won't find a nicer copy that this of the scarce promo! Condition: NM 8 (original Vee-Jay sleeve)/ NM 8 (side 1)/ MT 9 (side 2).

**Beatles "From Me to You/ Thank You Girl" Rare Label 45 (Vee-Jay 522, 1963).** From the pre-Beatlemania days - at least in the US - is this 1963 release, which was pressed in three different label versions. This one is the black label with silver horizontal lines. Condition: VG-EX 6, and in a vintage Vee-Jay sleeve.
**Beatles "Please Please Me" Promo 45 and Rare Sleeve (Vee-Jay 581, 1964).** The original US pressing of "Please Please Me"/ "From Me To You" (Vee-Jay 498, 1963) didn't cause a stir, but when Beatlemania hit with full force in early 1964, Vee-Jay's second pressing met with much greater success. Vee-Jay issued a sleeve with the promo proclaiming this to be "The Record That Started Beatlemania!" The actual recording did precede the Fab's first two #1 US singles "I Want to Hold Your Hand" and "She Loves You", but didn't peak in the US until after those two had established a foothold on the #1 Billboard Top 100 charts in early 1964. The sleeve is rarer and more valuable than the promo disc. Condition: VG 5 (price sticker on one side, small amount of writing ["Rec"] on the other)/ VG-EX 6 ("Please Please Me" side has some tape residue on the label).
**Beatles "Please Please Me/ From Me To You" Promo Single (Vee-Jay 581, 1964).** Immaculate copy of the rare blue and white label promo. Condition: MT 9.

**Beatles****_Souvenir of Their Visit to America_****Rare "Ask Me Why**" **Promo Sleeve (Vee-Jay EPI-903, 1964).** When was the last time you saw a copy of _this_? If your answer is anything other than "Never!" you're in a distinct minority! Chances are, at best you've only heard about it. This black and white sleeve was issued with some later promotional copies of the Vee-Jay EP as part of a marketing campaign touting a new lower price. An odd feature is its opening at the bottom. Super-rare! Condition: EX 7.5 (sleeve only).
**Beatles****_Souvenir of Their Visit to America_****Sealed EP (Vee-Jay 1-003, 1964).** What a find! Sealed copies of the Fab Four's first EP are just about non-existent. None other than Beatles know-it-all Perry Cox estimates "only a couple of known factory-sealed examples are known to exist." No need to look any further! Condition: Still sealed NM 8 (sleeve)/ Still sealed GM-MT 10 (disc). _LOA from Perry Cox._
**Beatles "She Loves You/ I'll Get You" Promo Single (Swan 4152, 1963).** Although it was recorded in 1963, it probably wasn't the first song an American teen heard in 1964 from the new (to the US) band. But it was quickly one of the most popular. Fine copy of the white label promo. Condition: EX 7 with "X" on A side label.
**Beatles "Can't Buy Me Love/ You Can't Do That" Acetate (Capitol, 1964).** Rare 8" acetate of one of the band's biggest two-sided hits from early in the Beatlemania year of 1964. "Can't Buy Me Love" was the fourth biggest Fab single ever, ruling the charts for five weeks. Master Nos. X44913 and -914 are indicated. Condition: EX 7.

**_Meet The Beatles_****Promo Open-End Interview Compact 33 (Capitol Pro 2548, 1964).** This is the first time we've seen a copy of this specially-made for radio promotion of the Fab's first Capitol release. The 7" disc featured a few minutes of interviews, plus three songs from the album, "I Want To Hold Your Hand, This Boy, and It Won't Be Long." Condition: VG 5 (sleeve)/ EX 7.
**_The Beatles' Second_****_Album_****Rare Promo Open-End Interview Compact 33 (Capitol Pro 2599).** This rare 7" 33 1/3 rpm disc features an interview with the Fab and three selections from their second Capitol album, "Roll Over Beethoven, Please Mr. Postman, and Thank You Girl." Condition: VG-EX 6.5 (cover)/ MT 9 (disc).
**Beatles****_Help!_****Red Vinyl Stereo LP With OBI (Japan - Odeon OP7387, 1965).** The Fab Four disproved any naysayers' predictions that 1964 was a flash in the pan by an equally triumphant 1965. Four albums released in 1965 promptly went to #1, including this soundtrack album which stayed on top for nine weeks. Attesting to their worldwide popularity is this Japanese copy with its original OBI. Condition: EX 7 (some tanning on inside gatefold)/ EX 7 (original pressing red vinyl).

**Beatles - John Lennon "Imagine" Record Award (Apple 1840, 1971**). Lennon's timeless call for world peace, described by him as: "Anti-religious, anti-nationalistic, anti-conventional, [and] anti-capitalistic." There is a plaque beneath the gold disc on this in-house award stating: "'Imagine All The People' Thanks A Million J & Y". Disc and plaque Excellent, the frame has some scratches and flaws.
**Beatles - John Lennon / Yoko Ono****_Double Fantasy_****RIAA Platinum Record Award.** The last studio recordings released in John Lennon's lifetime were included on _Double Fantasy_, created in collaboration and full partnership with his wife Yoko Ono. The couple had begun the recording in the late summer of 1980, in secret and without having signed with a label. After they were were satisfied that the content was strong, their publicist leaked the news and they were immediately inundated with offers from all of the major labels. David Geffen had only launched his namesake label that same year, but he purportedly sealed the deal for _Double Fantasy_ by approaching Yoko first, assuring the couple that he considered her contributions as equal to John's - even before Geffen had heard any of the recordings. The LP went on to win the 1981 Grammy Award for Album of The Year.
This RIAA-certified platinum sales award reads "Presented to Geffen Records to Commemorate the Sale of More Than 1,000,000 copies of the Geffen Records Long Playing Record Album "Double Fantasy." It is a beautiful display piece, in overall Very Good condition with some scuffs to the plexiglass and small dings to the distressed-silver wooden frame, which measures approximately 21" x 17".

**Beatles - John and Cynthia Lennon Owned Glass Vase From Kenwood, 1965.** John and Cynthia lived in the country home known as Kenwood from 1964 until 1968. Although their marriage ended in divorce, there were many happy times had there, and the Lennon estate was very near the home of Ringo and Maureen Starr known as Sunny Heights. The vase offered here was purchased by John and Cynthia while on holiday with the Starrs in 1965. It is Italian glass of flattened bottle form, orange and yellow cased in clear glass, 18" high. In overall Very Good condition with a small chip at the bottom. _Includes a handwritten COA from Cynthia Lennon which reads: "This ornament was bought by John and myself (along with another in the shape of a fish which has since been broken). We bought it on the holiday island of St. Vincent with Maureen & Ringo (Starr). It took pride of place in our bedroom at Kenwood. C. Lennon"_
Provenance: Christie's Pop and Guitars sale number 7322, London, 5 September 1996, Lot 443.
**Beatles - John Lennon****_Imagine_****Promo Store Display (1971**). A 12.25" square glossy album slick of the legendary Lennon album on white cardboard. The back has a fold-out easel and a pull-up hanging tab giving the record store a choice between hanging it or setting it on a shelf or counter. VG-EX 6.

**Beatles Related - A Bagism Performance Bag From Yoko Ono, circa late 1960s.** John and Yoko publicly introduced the concept of Bagism at a March 1969 press conference in Vienna, although they'd appeared in a bag performance piece in late 1968 at an artists gathering held at the Royal Albert Hall. Ono's background in performance art predated her involvement with Lennon - she'd been involved with the New York art scene since the early 1960s, and had received great attention for _Cut Piece_, which she debuted in 1964 and famously performed at Carnegie Hall in 1965. And while _Cut Piece_ hinged on the removal of the clothing which covers one's body, Bagism literally involved wearing a bag over one's entire body to shade the individual from any preconceptions based on race, gender, appearance, etc. By doing so, the idea was that "pure communication" could be achieved.
This very rare lot is a black cotton bag which came to it's original owner through Yoko Ono, likely in the late 1960s. The owner attended a party also attended by Ono and expressed interest in acquiring one of her bags for the purpose of meditation, which was later arranged and the bag delivered. It is in Excellent condition, sewn on three sides and without tags or labels, and measuring 67" x 51". _Includes a letter of provenance from the original owner who obtained the bag through Ono._
Provenance: Christie's Pop Memorabilia Sale 4388; London, 29 August 1991; Lot 556
**Beatles - Paul McCartney Signed Hofner Bass Guitar.** A B Bass Icon Series Hofner four string electric bass, strung left-handed and signed in 2007 on the pearloid pickguard in black marker. Excellent condition, with hardshell case. _LOAs from Perry Cox and Frank Caiazzo._

**Beatles - Paul McCartney Signed Color Tour Book Page.** An 8.75" x 11.75" color promo ad from the New World Tour book for the album _Off the Ground_ picturing the entire band and signed in silver felt tip by McCartney. The autograph was obtained on June 3, 2007, in New York City. Excellent. _COA From Heritage Auctions._
**Paul McCartney and Michael Jackson****_Say Say Say_****Signed 45 Record Sleeve (Columbia 38-04168, 1983).** This second single from the two superstars was released in October 1983, which was definitely a great year for Michael Jackson - in addition to singles from _Thriller,_ he chalked up his seventh #1 of the year with the release of this terrific duet. It also holds the distinction of being the release that put Paul McCartney atop the singles chart for the last time in the US. Produced by George Martin, and taken from Paul's _Pipes of Peace_ LP, this picture sleeve is signed boldly in blue marker by McCartney and black marker by Jackson. Condition: EX 7 (sleeve) / NM 8 (disc). _With PSA/DNA sticker affixed to the sleeve._
**Beatles - Paul McCartney Signed Book:****_Yesterday, The Beatles 1963-1965_****by Robert Freeman**. (New York: Holt Rinehart and Winston, 1983), first American edition, first printing, 10.25" x 9.25". The front cover of this glossy hard cover book features a color shot from the _Beatles for Sale_ session and is signed by McCartney in blue felt tip. Robert Freeman was the favorite photographer of the Beatles during the early days of their worldwide fame. He shot the cover photos for five of their UK Parlophone albums: _With the Beatles_, _Hard Day's Night_, _Beatles for Sale_, _Help!_, and _Rubber Soul_, as well as John Lennon's first two book covers. Very Good condition. _COA From Heritage Auctions._
**Paul McCartney Signed Baseball.** A Rawlings Official Major League Baseball with a bold "_Paul McCartney_" signature in blue felt tip on the sweet spot. Perfect for either Beatles or sports collectors. Excellent. _COA From Heritage Auctions._

**Beatles - Paul McCartney & Wings****_Band on the Run_****RIAA White Mat Gold Record Award (Apple SO-3415, 1973).** The last album McCartney issued on the Apple label and winner of the 1975 Grammy Award for "Best Pop Vocal Performance By a Duo, Group or Chorus." According to the plaque beneath the gold disc, this award was "Presented to Paul McCartney & Wings to Commemorate the Sale of More Than One Million Dollars Worth of the Apple Records Long-Playing Record Album 'Band On The Run'". Don't miss out on this one! Framed to an overall 17.5" x 21.5" and in Excellent condition.
**Beatles - Paul McCartney "Put It There" White Label Promo 45 Single (Capitol 7PRO-79074, 1989).** Brilliant copy of an ultra-rare promo. How rare? Noted Beatles expert Perry Cox estimates a mere 5-6 exist! The uncharted tune - on both sides of the disc - is from Sir Paul's _Flowers In The Dirt_ LP. Condition: MT 9 (original sleeve)/ MT 9 (disc).
**Beatles - Paul McCartney "Another Day" 10" One-sided Acetate (US - Apple, 1971)** Sir Paul's first solo single following the Beatles breakup was released on February 19, 1971. This acetate version was produced in very limited numbers, and this one's a nice copy. Condition: EX 7

**_Dylan in Woodstock_****by Elliot Landy Deluxe Limited Edition Book #75/100 (Genesis Publications, 2000).** This lavish book contains some of the most intimate photos of the oft-reclusive Bob Dylan ever seen. The 144 pages are filled with Elliot Landy's informal and atmospheric images of Bob Dylan, as he retreated from his first wave of worldwide fame, to live a quiet country life in 1966 with his new wife. Along the way, he reinvents himself musically with help from the Band. The book is as beautiful on the outside as the photos inside, with a supple brown suede binding, gilded page edging, and a slipcover. Included is an additional packet containing a color photo, signed by Landy. A rare book with some very minor handling wear; otherwise in Excellent condition.
**Bob Dylan****_Thin Wild Mercury: Touching Dylan's Edge_****Deluxe Limited Edition Book #85/1500 (Genesis Publications, 2006).** Jerry Schatzberg wrote this award-winning book covering several hundred photos of Dylan, taken by Schatzberg, many of which are previously unreleased, into 294 leather-bound pages, with silver edging, all housed in a cloth bound slipcase, with an extra art print signed by the author, and a cloth bag in which to store the book. All are in Excellent condition. The original shipping box is included.

**Eagles Autographed First Album,****_Eagles_****(Asylum SD-5054, 1972)** The Eagles' self-titled debut album laid the groundwork for what would become a very dominant strain of American popular music in the 1970s: melodic California based country-infused rock that was not too hard and not too soft. The album's lead track and first single, "Take It Easy," can be seen as a manifesto of the movement, and was listed as one of "The 500 Songs That Shaped Rock & Roll" by the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. This copy of the LP has been beautifully signed on the front cover by the original band members Don Henley, Joe Walsh (both in black marker), Glen Frey, Don Felder (both in blue marker), and Randy Meisner (in blue ink). The signatures have been dated to the 1990s. The LP has been matted for framing by the current owner, which is how it is being offered here. In Excellent condition. _COA from Perry Cox._

**Everly Brothers****_Terry Slater_****Stage Played Bass With Original Hardcase (Gibson, c. 1963).** A _circa_ 1963 Cherry Red Gibson EB3 bass, given by Chet Atkins (who originally purchased the bass) to Terry Slater, guitarist and/or bass player with such musical royalty as Little Richard, Jerry Lee Lewis, Duane Eddy, Bo Diddley, Muddy Waters, Chuck Berry, The Rolling Stones, Gene Vincent, Ray Charles, and more. Terry used this bass on every single recording that he ever did with the Everly Brothers. He also played the bass for Eric Burden (The Animals) and Glen Campbell, and as the story goes, they would all trade off instruments during their jam sessions, so this bass has been played by many famous people. When Terry stopped playing for the Everly's, he put the bass up, and it has been in storage ever since, until he graciously let us place it in this auction for you to bid on. The bass comes in its original case (one latch is missing), with normal wear for a touring bass case. The guitar is in very nice shape for a well used professional instrument. There are a few small dings and scratches on the neck and the body, some chrome loss from finger wear on the neck pickup, and oxidization on the bridge pickup; otherwise in Excellent condition. A true piece of Rock and Roll history!

**Carl Donnell "Kansas" Fields Passport Signed by Frank Sinatra Plus A Billie Holiday Handwritten Letter, 1950s.** "Kansas" Fields was a Jazz drummer, beginning in Chicago in the late 1920s; he played with Cab Calloway, Sidney Bechet, Dizzie Gillespie, Ella Fitzgerald, and more, and recorded with John Coltrane and Kenny Burrell in the 1950s.. Here's his passport from 1952, featuring numerous stamps from countries he visited plus his signature in three different places. Additional signatures of Frank Sinatra and Ava Gardner appear on page 8; and a Christmas card Billie Holiday sent to the drummer is included, handwritten in black ballpoint ink, reading in part"Hey Kansas / What's happening / with my trunk... / I've / got to have those / things. / Have a Merry Christmas / Lady Day."Also included is a small flyer from a French nightclub dated 1953 noting Frank Sinatra's name -- interestingly, the date on this flyer is the day that Sinatra, Gardner, Holiday and Fields met. Items are 4" x 9.5" and smaller; Very Good condition overall.
**Peter Frampton****_Frampton Comes Alive_****Platinum Record Award (A&M SP-3703, 1976).** A double-record set recorded live, this was the top-selling album for all of 1976 and one of the best sellers of all time with current worldwide sales of over eleven million. According to the plaque beneath the platinum disc on this in-house award, it was "Presented to Bob Scharbert For Helping Make the Peter Frampton Album 'Frampton Comes Alive' Sell Over a Million Copies by A & M Records". Scharbert was an employee of A&M Records. Framed to an overall 16" x 16" and in Excellent condition.

**Art Garfunkel****_Watermark_****RIAA Gold Record Award (Columbia JC 34975, 1977).** His third solo album which included the hit single "(What a) Wonderful World" where James Taylor and his former partner Paul Simon sang harmonies. According to the plaque beneath the gold disc, this award was "Presented to Columbia Records to Commemorate the Sale of More Than 500,000 Copies of the Columbia Records Long-Playing Record Album 'Watermark'". **Beatles Autographed Postcard With Jimmie Nichol Signature, 1964.** John, Paul, George, and...Jimmie? On the day before the start of the Beatles' 1964 tour of Europe and the Far East, Ringo suddenly came down with tonsillitis and was admitted to a London hospital. With little time to spare, Brian Epstein enlisted George Martin to help find a replacement. Martin had the ideal candidate, a talented young drummer named Jimmie Nichol, whom he knew from a recent Tommy Quickly session. Nichol duly had one practice session with the the other three, and 27 hours later was taking the stage with them for the first tour date in Copenhagen on June 4. After his surgery and recuperation, Ringo rejoined the others onstage on June 15 in Australia, and Nichol's 11 days in the most famous pop group in history came to an end. Jimmie was apparently the first to sign this BOAC postcard of London, writing "To Lynne, Best Wishes, Jimmie Nichol" followed by Paul, John, and George, all in bold black ink. In overall Very Good condition, some creases and an apparent fold at center, and two sets of staple holes in one corner. _COA from Frank Caiazzo._
**Beatles Group Autographed Photo Including Both Ringo Starr and Pete Best Signatures.** This vintage photograph of the Beatles was taken in late 1961, when the group was still sporting the black leather look adopted in Hamburg and Pete Best was still the drummer. The back of the photo was signed in late 1962 by the group, however, after Best had been replaced by Ringo Starr. John, Paul, George, and Ringo have all signed boldly in black ink, with John and Paul adding "Love", and all four adding "XXX," which was common in the early days. Pete Best's signature was added later in blue ink, making this a truly rare collection of Beatle autographs. In Very Good condition, with some slight edge wear and several small stains, and several small scratches to the frame. The piece has been nicely matted with a Ringo-lineup custom matte to the front, and a cutaway to the back allowing viewing of the Best-lineup photo. _COA from Tracks, LTD._

Beatles Autographed _Beatles For Sale_ Albums Here is a fantastic presentation piece which is a terrifically clever display of the Beatles' fourth album _Beatles For Sale._ Within the framed display are two separate copies of the LP which together contain a full set of signatures of all four of the Beatles, and allows for enjoyment of both sides of the album artwork. To the left on the color cover photograph by Robert Freeman are bold black signatures rendered in felt tip by John, Ringo, and Paul, just above their respective images. To the right, George has written "Best Wishes from George Harrison" in black ballpoint next to his image of the group in performance at their first US concert at the Washington Coliseum. The overall impact of the two covers together is quite stunning, and is simply one of the best displays of Beatle signatures we've ever seen. Also presented is side one of the LP, all three elements matted within a black composite frame measuring approximately 34" x 34". _COA from Frank Caiazzo, dating both signature pieces to early 1965._
**Beatles Set Of Autographs, 1963.**
Here is as beautiful and as straightforward a set of early Beatles autographs as one could hope for. Signed on a light blue page taken from an autograph book are all four signatures in bold blue ink. Ringo has added "The Beatles" just above his signature at top, and added his "star" line below. The autograph sheet measures approximately 4" x 6" and is in Excellent condition. It is presented beneath a very sharp 10.5" x 13" photograph of the Beatles performing for television in 1963, both professionally matted and in a black wooden frame measuring 21.5" x 19". _COA from Perry Cox._

**Beatles Autographs On British Governmental Stationery, Early 1960s.** This fine set of Beatles autographs dates to the early 1960s, and were purportedly obtained by a British air transit officer when the group returned to the UK from an overseas tour. That would seem quite plausible, as the signatures are affixed to a piece of ruled paper which bears the crest of the British government. The sheet is 12.75" x 8" overall, and had likely been folded in half, lengthwise, when presented to the Beatles for signing, as the autographs are neatly centered on the right half of the page. Paul has signed at top in bold blue ink, and the other three have added their autographs in black ink. The paper is in Very Good condition, with some yellowing from age and folded lengthwise as mentioned, and with an additional horizontal and vertical fold. There is an approximate 1" tear through the horizontal fold, front and back, which does go through the crest but does not impact the autographs._COA From Heritage Auctions._
**Beatles: Signatures of John, Paul, and Ringo on a Postcard Obtained During the****_Magical Mystery Tour_****Filming, with Four Color Snapshots.** A 6" x 4" color glossy postcard of "Watergate Bay, near Newquay, Cornwall" signed on the message side by three in ink: "_To Anne love from John Lennon_", "_Paul McCartney_", and "_Ringo Starr_". The Beatles and their tour bus pulled up at the Atlantic Hotel in Newquay on the evening of September 12, 1967, intending to stay one night. They ended up spending three nights at the hotel and filmed various scenes in the area. These autographs were obtained at the hotel, possibly on the 13th when George was unavailable for filming while he was giving an extensive interview to the BBC. Beatle autographs from 1967 are much rarer than earlier examples. The signatures are a bit light but clear and legible, overall Fine condition. _COA from Tracks LTD._
Also included are four 3.5" square color candid snapshots, one of each Beatle, taken at the same hotel during the above-mentioned dates. Excellent.

**Beatles Fully Autographed Cavern Club Booklet, Including Both Ringo Starr and Pete Best** This vintage 1963 Season Cavern Club membership booklet and additional pages from a similar 1961 booklet gave the young fan who owned it the rare distinction of having signatures by five members of the Beatles, namely John, Paul, George, Ringo, and the group's original drummer, Pete Best.
The signatures are featured on several pages within the booklet and on pages from a 1961 version of the booklet, and were obtained by a young fan in Liverpool named Sheila Stewart. One signed page bears the inscriptions "To Sheila love from John Lennon X" and "To Sheila love from Paul McCartney XXX" in blue ink. Another bears signatures in red ink from McCartney, Starr, Best, and Gerry Marsden of Gerry & The Pacemakers, with Starr adding "The Sensational" and "DRUM" to his autograph. George Harrison signed on the following page in red ballpoint, and Best inscribed "Lots of Love to Sheila Pete Best XXX" in red ink.
A great collection of Beatles signatures, signed while on the cusp of celebrity. Signed Cavern Club membership books are very rare, and few signed by the Beatles are known to exist. The presence of Best's signature makes this even more desirable.
The booklet measures approximately 4.5" x 2" when closed, and exhibits expected wear. In overall Very Good condition, with some slight edgewear, creases, and small stains. _LOA from Frank Caiazzo._

**Beatles (as Tony Sheridan and The Beat Brothers) "My Bonnie/ The Saints" Promo 45 (Decca 31382, 1962).** One of the most important vinyl discs ever produced is this innocuous pink label promo recording on the familiar Decca label. It was all but ignored in the US where this was released, as were the Beatles in general in 1962. The Fab were beginning to make a name for themselves in their Liverpool hometown and garnering a following in the unlikely locale of Hamburg, Germany, where they worked alongside fellow Brit, Tony Sheridan. When Polydor signed Sheridan, the label selected the Beatles to back him on a single, calling the group "The Beat Brothers" to avoid tricky translation problems. The two Tin Pan Alley standards that were recorded were released to some success -- but only in Germany. Decca, an American affiliate of Polydor, issued pink label promo copies and black label commercial copies in the States to absolutely no avail! America wasn't ready for the British Invasion in 1962! It would be two years later in 1964, after the launch of Beatlemania in the US, that MGM would reissue this single, and only then did the record, now credited solely to The Beatles, enjoy commercial success. The Decca version is the very first American release by the Beatles, whose name doesn't even appear on the label! Rare without question, and in this condition practically unique. Condition: MT 9.
**Beatles ("Beattles") "Please Please Me/ Ask My Why" Rare Promo 45 (Vee-Jay 498, 1963).** The second rarest Vee-Jay promo single comes in two versions: one with the group's name spelled correctly, another - as offered here - with the Fab's name misspelled "Beattles". You won't find a nicer copy that this of the scarce promo! Condition: NM 8 (original Vee-Jay sleeve)/ NM 8 (side 1)/ MT 9 (side 2).

**Beatles "From Me to You/ Thank You Girl" Rare Label 45 (Vee-Jay 522, 1963).** From the pre-Beatlemania days - at least in the US - is this 1963 release, which was pressed in three different label versions. This one is the black label with silver horizontal lines. Condition: VG-EX 6, and in a vintage Vee-Jay sleeve.
**Beatles "Please Please Me" Promo 45 and Rare Sleeve (Vee-Jay 581, 1964).** The original US pressing of "Please Please Me"/ "From Me To You" (Vee-Jay 498, 1963) didn't cause a stir, but when Beatlemania hit with full force in early 1964, Vee-Jay's second pressing met with much greater success. Vee-Jay issued a sleeve with the promo proclaiming this to be "The Record That Started Beatlemania!" The actual recording did precede the Fab's first two #1 US singles "I Want to Hold Your Hand" and "She Loves You", but didn't peak in the US until after those two had established a foothold on the #1 Billboard Top 100 charts in early 1964. The sleeve is rarer and more valuable than the promo disc. Condition: VG 5 (price sticker on one side, small amount of writing ["Rec"] on the other)/ VG-EX 6 ("Please Please Me" side has some tape residue on the label).
**Beatles "Please Please Me/ From Me To You" Promo Single (Vee-Jay 581, 1964).** Immaculate copy of the rare blue and white label promo. Condition: MT 9.

**Beatles****_Souvenir of Their Visit to America_****Rare "Ask Me Why**" **Promo Sleeve (Vee-Jay EPI-903, 1964).** When was the last time you saw a copy of _this_? If your answer is anything other than "Never!" you're in a distinct minority! Chances are, at best you've only heard about it. This black and white sleeve was issued with some later promotional copies of the Vee-Jay EP as part of a marketing campaign touting a new lower price. An odd feature is its opening at the bottom. Super-rare! Condition: EX 7.5 (sleeve only).
**Beatles****_Souvenir of Their Visit to America_****Sealed EP (Vee-Jay 1-003, 1964).** What a find! Sealed copies of the Fab Four's first EP are just about non-existent. None other than Beatles know-it-all Perry Cox estimates "only a couple of known factory-sealed examples are known to exist." No need to look any further! Condition: Still sealed NM 8 (sleeve)/ Still sealed GM-MT 10 (disc). _LOA from Perry Cox._
**Beatles "She Loves You/ I'll Get You" Promo Single (Swan 4152, 1963).** Although it was recorded in 1963, it probably wasn't the first song an American teen heard in 1964 from the new (to the US) band. But it was quickly one of the most popular. Fine copy of the white label promo. Condition: EX 7 with "X" on A side label.
**Beatles "Can't Buy Me Love/ You Can't Do That" Acetate (Capitol, 1964).** Rare 8" acetate of one of the band's biggest two-sided hits from early in the Beatlemania year of 1964. "Can't Buy Me Love" was the fourth biggest Fab single ever, ruling the charts for five weeks. Master Nos. X44913 and -914 are indicated. Condition: EX 7.

**_Meet The Beatles_****Promo Open-End Interview Compact 33 (Capitol Pro 2548, 1964).** This is the first time we've seen a copy of this specially-made for radio promotion of the Fab's first Capitol release. The 7" disc featured a few minutes of interviews, plus three songs from the album, "I Want To Hold Your Hand, This Boy, and It Won't Be Long." Condition: VG 5 (sleeve)/ EX 7.

**Beatles****_Help!_****Red Vinyl Stereo LP With OBI (Japan - Odeon OP7387, 1965).** The Fab Four disproved any naysayers' predictions that 1964 was a flash in the pan by an equally triumphant 1965. **Beatles - John Lennon "Imagine" Record Award (Apple 1840, 1971**). Lennon's timeless call for world peace, described by him as: "Anti-religious, anti-nationalistic, anti-conventional, [and] anti-capitalistic." There is a plaque beneath the gold disc on this in-house award stating: "'Imagine All The People' Thanks A Million J & Y". Disc and plaque Excellent, the frame has some scratches and flaws.
**Beatles - John Lennon / Yoko Ono****_Double Fantasy_****RIAA Platinum Record Award.** The last studio recordings released in John Lennon's lifetime were included on _Double Fantasy_, created in collaboration and full partnership with his wife Yoko Ono. The couple had begun the recording in the late summer of 1980, in secret and without having signed with a label. After they were were satisfied that the content was strong, their publicist leaked the news and they were immediately inundated with offers from all of the major labels. David Geffen had only launched his namesake label that same year, but he purportedly sealed the deal for _Double Fantasy_ by approaching Yoko first, assuring the couple that he considered her contributions as equal to John's - even before Geffen had heard any of the recordings. The LP went on to win the 1981 Grammy Award for Album of The Year.
This RIAA-certified platinum sales award reads "Presented to Geffen Records to Commemorate the Sale of More Than 1,000,000 copies of the Geffen Records Long Playing Record Album "Double Fantasy." It is a beautiful display piece, in overall Very Good condition with some scuffs to the plexiglass and small dings to the distressed-silver wooden frame, which measures approximately 21" x 17".

**Beatles Related - A Bagism Performance Bag From Yoko Ono, circa late 1960s.** John and Yoko publicly introduced the concept of Bagism at a March 1969 press conference in Vienna, although they'd appeared in a bag performance piece in late 1968 at an artists gathering held at the Royal Albert Hall. Ono's background in performance art predated her involvement with Lennon - she'd been involved with the New York art scene since the early 1960s, and had received great attention for _Cut Piece_, which she debuted in 1964 and famously performed at Carnegie Hall in 1965. And while _Cut Piece_ hinged on the removal of the clothing which covers one's body, Bagism literally involved wearing a bag over one's entire body to shade the individual from any preconceptions based on race, gender, appearance, etc. By doing so, the idea was that "pure communication" could be achieved.
This very rare lot is a black cotton bag which came to it's original owner through Yoko Ono, likely in the late 1960s. The owner attended a party also attended by Ono and expressed interest in acquiring one of her bags for the purpose of meditation, which was later arranged and the bag delivered. It is in Excellent condition, sewn on three sides and without tags or labels, and measuring 67" x 51". _Includes a letter of provenance from the original owner who obtained the bag through Ono._
Provenance: Christie's Pop Memorabilia Sale 4388; London, 29 August 1991; Lot 556

**_Dylan in Woodstock_****by Elliot Landy Deluxe Limited Edition Book #75/100 (Genesis Publications, 2000).** This lavish book contains some of the most intimate photos of the oft-reclusive Bob Dylan ever seen. The 144 pages are filled with Elliot Landy's informal and atmospheric images of Bob Dylan, as he retreated from his first wave of worldwide fame, to live a quiet country life in 1966 with his new wife. Along the way, he reinvents himself musically with help from the Band. The book is as beautiful on the outside as the photos inside, with a supple brown suede binding, gilded page edging, and a slipcover. texts.213: **Eagles Autographed First Album,****_Eagles_****(Asylum SD-5054, 1972)** The Eagles' self-titled debut album laid the groundwork for what would become a very dominant strain of American popular music in the 1970s: melodic California based country-infused rock that was not too hard and not too soft. The album's lead track and first single, "Take It Easy," can be seen as a manifesto of the movement, and was listed as one of "The 500 Songs That Shaped Rock & Roll" by the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. This copy of the LP has been beautifully signed on the front cover by the original band members Don Henley, Joe Walsh (both in black marker), Glen Frey, Don Felder (both in blue marker), and Randy Meisner (in blue ink). The signatures have been dated to the 1990s. The LP has been matted for framing by the current owner, which is how it is being offered here. In Excellent condition. _COA from Perry Cox._
texts.214: **Everly Brothers****_Terry Slater_****Stage Played Bass With Original Hardcase (Gibson, c. 1963).** A _circa_ 1963 Cherry Red Gibson EB3 bass, given by Chet Atkins (who originally purchased the bass) to Terry Slater, guitarist and/or bass player with such musical royalty as Little Richard, Jerry Lee Lewis, Duane Eddy, Bo Diddley, Muddy Waters, Chuck Berry, The Rolling Stones, Gene Vincent, Ray Charles, and more. Terry used this bass on every single recording that he ever did with the Everly Brothers. He also played the bass for Eric Burden (The Animals) and Glen Campbell, and as the story goes, they would all trade off instruments during their jam sessions, so this bass has been played by many famous people. When Terry stopped playing for the Everly's, he put the bass up, and it has been in storage ever since, until he graciously let us place it in this auction for you to bid on. The bass comes in its original case (one latch is missing), with normal wear for a touring bass case. The guitar is in very nice shape for a well used professional instrument. There are a few small dings and scratches on the neck and the body, some chrome loss from finger wear on the neck pickup, and oxidization on the bridge pickup; otherwise in Excellent condition. A true piece of Rock and Roll history!

**Beatles Autographed Postcard With Jimmie Nichol Signature, 1964.** John, Paul, George, and...Jimmie? On the day before the start of the Beatles' 1964 tour of Europe and the Far East, Ringo suddenly came down with tonsillitis and was admitted to a London hospital. With little time to spare, Brian Epstein enlisted George Martin to help find a replacement. Martin had the ideal candidate, a talented young drummer named Jimmie Nichol, whom he knew from a recent Tommy Quickly session. Nichol duly had one practice session with the the other three, and 27 hours later was taking the stage with them for the first tour date in Copenhagen on June 4. After his surgery and recuperation, Ringo rejoined the others onstage on June 15 in Australia, and Nichol's 11 days in the most famous pop group in history came to an end. Jimmie was apparently the first to sign this BOAC postcard of London, writing "To Lynne, Best Wishes, Jimmie Nichol" followed by Paul, John, and George, all in bold black ink. In overall Very Good condition, some creases and an apparent fold at center, and two sets of staple holes in one corner. _COA from Frank Caiazzo._
**Beatles Group Autographed Photo Including Both Ringo Starr and Pete Best Signatures.** This vintage photograph of the Beatles was taken in late 1961, when the group was still sporting the black leather look adopted in Hamburg and Pete Best was still the drummer. The back of the photo was signed in late 1962 by the group, however, after Best had been replaced by Ringo Starr. John, Paul, George, and Ringo have all signed boldly in black ink, with John and Paul adding "Love", and all four adding "XXX," which was common in the early days. Pete Best's signature was added later in blue ink, making this a truly rare collection of Beatle autographs. In Very Good condition, with some slight edge wear and several small stains, and several small scratches to the frame. The piece has been nicely matted with a Ringo-lineup custom matte to the front, and a cutaway to the back allowing viewing of the Best-lineup photo. _COA from Tracks, LTD._

Beatles Autographed _Beatles For Sale_ Albums Here is a fantastic presentation piece which is a terrifically clever display of the Beatles' fourth album _Beatles For Sale._ Within the framed display are two separate copies of the LP which together contain a full set of signatures of all four of the Beatles, and allows for enjoyment of both sides of the album artwork. To the left on the color cover photograph by Robert Freeman are bold black signatures rendered in felt tip by John, Ringo, and Paul, just above their respective images. To the right, George has written "Best Wishes from George Harrison" in black ballpoint next to his image of the group in performance at their first US concert at the Washington Coliseum. The overall impact of the two covers together is quite stunning, and is simply one of the best displays of Beatle signatures we've ever seen. Also presented is side one of the LP, all three elements matted within a black composite frame measuring approximately 34" x 34". _COA from Frank Caiazzo, dating both signature pieces to early 1965._
**Beatles Set Of Autographs, 1963.**
Here is as beautiful and as straightforward a set of early Beatles autographs as one could hope for. Signed on a light blue page taken from an autograph book are all four signatures in bold blue ink. Ringo has added "The Beatles" just above his signature at top, and added his "star" line below. The autograph sheet measures approximately 4" x 6" and is in Excellent condition. It is presented beneath a very sharp 10.5" x 13" photograph of the Beatles performing for television in 1963, both professionally matted and in a black wooden frame measuring 21.5" x 19". _COA from Perry Cox._

**Beatles Autographs On British Governmental Stationery, Early 1960s.** This fine set of Beatles autographs dates to the early 1960s, and were purportedly obtained by a British air transit officer when the group returned to the UK from an overseas tour. That would seem quite plausible, as the signatures are affixed to a piece of ruled paper which bears the crest of the British government. The sheet is 12.75" x 8" overall, and had likely been folded in half, lengthwise, when presented to the Beatles for signing, as the autographs are neatly centered on the right half of the page. Paul has signed at top in bold blue ink, and the other three have added their autographs in black ink. The paper is in Very Good condition, with some yellowing from age and folded lengthwise as mentioned, and with an additional horizontal and vertical fold. There is an approximate 1" tear through the horizontal fold, front and back, which does go through the crest but does not impact the autographs._COA From Heritage Auctions._
**Beatles: Signatures of John, Paul, and Ringo on a Postcard Obtained During the****_Magical Mystery Tour_****Filming, with Four Color Snapshots.** A 6" x 4" color glossy postcard of "Watergate Bay, near Newquay, Cornwall" signed on the message side by three in ink: "_To Anne love from John Lennon_", "_Paul McCartney_", and "_Ringo Starr_". The Beatles and their tour bus pulled up at the Atlantic Hotel in Newquay on the evening of September 12, 1967, intending to stay one night. They ended up spending three nights at the hotel and filmed various scenes in the area. These autographs were obtained at the hotel, possibly on the 13th when George was unavailable for filming while he was giving an extensive interview to the BBC. Beatle autographs from 1967 are much rarer than earlier examples. The signatures are a bit light but clear and legible, overall Fine condition. _COA from Tracks LTD._
Also included are four 3.5" square color candid snapshots, one of each Beatle, taken at the same hotel during the above-mentioned dates. Excellent.

**Beatles Fully Autographed Cavern Club Booklet, Including Both Ringo Starr and Pete Best** This vintage 1963 Season Cavern Club membership booklet and additional pages from a similar 1961 booklet gave the young fan who owned it the rare distinction of having signatures by five members of the Beatles, namely John, Paul, George, Ringo, and the group's original drummer, Pete Best.
The signatures are featured on several pages within the booklet and on pages from a 1961 version of the booklet, and were obtained by a young fan in Liverpool named Sheila Stewart. One signed page bears the inscriptions "To Sheila love from John Lennon X" and "To Sheila love from Paul McCartney XXX" in blue ink. Another bears signatures in red ink from McCartney, Starr, Best, and Gerry Marsden of Gerry & The Pacemakers, with Starr adding "The Sensational" and "DRUM" to his autograph. George Harrison signed on the following page in red ballpoint, and Best inscribed "Lots of Love to Sheila Pete Best XXX" in red ink.
A great collection of Beatles signatures, signed while on the cusp of celebrity. Signed Cavern Club membership books are very rare, and few signed by the Beatles are known to exist. The presence of Best's signature makes this even more desirable.
The booklet measures approximately 4.5" x 2" when closed, and exhibits expected wear. In overall Very Good condition, with some slight edgewear, creases, and small stains. _LOA from Frank Caiazzo._

**Beatles (as Tony Sheridan and The Beat Brothers) "My Bonnie/ The Saints" Promo 45 (Decca 31382, 1962).** One of the most important vinyl discs ever produced is this innocuous pink label promo recording on the familiar Decca label. It was all but ignored in the US where this was released, as were the Beatles in general in 1962. The Fab were beginning to make a name for themselves in their Liverpool hometown and garnering a following in the unlikely locale of Hamburg, Germany, where they worked alongside fellow Brit, Tony Sheridan. When Polydor signed Sheridan, the label selected the Beatles to back him on a single, calling the group "The Beat Brothers" to avoid tricky translation problems. The two Tin Pan Alley standards that were recorded were released to some success -- but only in Germany. Decca, an American affiliate of Polydor, issued pink label promo copies and black label commercial copies in the States to absolutely no avail! America wasn't ready for the British Invasion in 1962! It would be two years later in 1964, after the launch of Beatlemania in the US, that MGM would reissue this single, and only then did the record, now credited solely to The Beatles, enjoy commercial success. The Decca version is the very first American release by the Beatles, whose name doesn't even appear on the label! Rare without question, and in this condition practically unique. Condition: MT 9.
**Beatles ("Beattles") "Please Please Me/ Ask My Why" Rare Promo 45 (Vee-Jay 498, 1963).** The second rarest Vee-Jay promo single comes in two versions: one with the group's name spelled correctly, another - as offered here - with the Fab's name misspelled "Beattles". You won't find a nicer copy that this of the scarce promo! Condition: NM 8 (original Vee-Jay sleeve)/ NM 8 (side 1)/ MT 9 (side 2).

**Beatles "From Me to You/ Thank You Girl" Rare Label 45 (Vee-Jay 522, 1963).** From the pre-Beatlemania days - at least in the US - is this 1963 release, which was pressed in three different label versions. This one is the black label with silver horizontal lines. Condition: VG-EX 6, and in a vintage Vee-Jay sleeve.
**Beatles "Please Please Me" Promo 45 and Rare Sleeve (Vee-Jay 581, 1964).** The original US pressing of "Please Please Me"/ "From Me To You" (Vee-Jay 498, 1963) didn't cause a stir, but when Beatlemania hit with full force in early 1964, Vee-Jay's second pressing met with much greater success. Vee-Jay issued a sleeve with the promo proclaiming this to be "The Record That Started Beatlemania!" The actual recording did precede the Fab's first two #1 US singles "I Want to Hold Your Hand" and "She Loves You", but didn't peak in the US until after those two had established a foothold on the #1 Billboard Top 100 charts in early 1964. The sleeve is rarer and more valuable than the promo disc. Condition: VG 5 (price sticker on one side, small amount of writing ["Rec"] on the other)/ VG-EX 6 ("Please Please Me" side has some tape residue on the label).
**Beatles "Please Please Me/ From Me To You" Promo Single (Vee-Jay 581, 1964).** Immaculate copy of the rare blue and white label promo. Condition: MT 9.

**Beatles****_Souvenir of Their Visit to America_****Rare "Ask Me Why**" **Promo Sleeve (Vee-Jay EPI-903, 1964).** When was the last time you saw a copy of _this_? If your answer is anything other than "Never!" you're in a distinct minority! Chances are, at best you've only heard about it. This black and white sleeve was issued with some later promotional copies of the Vee-Jay EP as part of a marketing campaign touting a new lower price. An odd feature is its opening at the bottom. Super-rare! Condition: EX 7.5 (sleeve only).
**Beatles****_Souvenir of Their Visit to America_****Sealed EP (Vee-Jay 1-003, 1964).** What a find! Sealed copies of the Fab Four's first EP are just about non-existent. None other than Beatles know-it-all Perry Cox estimates "only a couple of known factory-sealed examples are known to exist." No need to look any further! Condition: Still sealed NM 8 (sleeve)/ Still sealed GM-MT 10 (disc). _LOA from Perry Cox._
**Beatles "She Loves You/ I'll Get You" Promo Single (Swan 4152, 1963).** Although it was recorded in 1963, it probably wasn't the first song an American teen heard in 1964 from the new (to the US) band. But it was quickly one of the most popular. Fine copy of the white label promo. Condition: EX 7 with "X" on A side label.
**Beatles "Can't Buy Me Love/ You Can't Do That" Acetate (Capitol, 1964).** Rare 8" acetate of one of the band's biggest two-sided hits from early in the Beatlemania year of 1964. "Can't Buy Me Love" was the fourth biggest Fab single ever, ruling the charts for five weeks. Master Nos. X44913 and -914 are indicated. Condition: EX 7.

**_Meet The Beatles_****Promo Open-End Interview Compact 33 (Capitol Pro 2548, 1964).** This is the first time we've seen a copy of this specially-made for radio promotion of the Fab's first Capitol release. The 7" disc featured a few minutes of interviews, plus three songs from the album, "I Want To Hold Your Hand, This Boy, and It Won't Be Long." Condition: VG 5 (sleeve)/ EX 7.
**_The Beatles' Second_****_Album_****Rare Promo Open-End Interview Compact 33 (Capitol Pro 2599).** This rare 7" 33 1/3 rpm disc features an interview with the Fab and three selections from their second Capitol album, "Roll Over Beethoven, Please Mr. Postman, and Thank You Girl." Condition: VG-EX 6.5 (cover)/ MT 9 (disc).
**Beatles****_Help!_****Red Vinyl Stereo LP With OBI (Japan - Odeon OP7387, 1965).** The Fab Four disproved any naysayers' predictions that 1964 was a flash in the pan by an equally triumphant 1965. Four albums released in 1965 promptly went to #1, including this soundtrack album which stayed on top for nine weeks. Attesting to their worldwide popularity is this Japanese copy with its original OBI. Condition: EX 7 (some tanning on inside gatefold)/ EX 7 (original pressing red vinyl).

**Beatles - John Lennon "Imagine" Record Award (Apple 1840, 1971**). Lennon's timeless call for world peace, described by him as: "Anti-religious, anti-nationalistic, anti-conventional, [and] anti-capitalistic." There is a plaque beneath the gold disc on this in-house award stating: "'Imagine All The People' Thanks A Million J & Y". Disc and plaque Excellent, the frame has some scratches and flaws.
**Beatles - John Lennon / Yoko Ono****_Double Fantasy_****RIAA Platinum Record Award.** The last studio recordings released in John Lennon's lifetime were included on _Double Fantasy_, created in collaboration and full partnership with his wife Yoko Ono. The couple had begun the recording in the late summer of 1980, in secret and without having signed with a label. After they were were satisfied that the content was strong, their publicist leaked the news and they were immediately inundated with offers from all of the major labels. David Geffen had only launched his namesake label that same year, but he purportedly sealed the deal for _Double Fantasy_ by approaching Yoko first, assuring the couple that he considered her contributions as equal to John's - even before Geffen had heard any of the recordings. The LP went on to win the 1981 Grammy Award for Album of The Year.
This RIAA-certified platinum sales award reads "Presented to Geffen Records to Commemorate the Sale of More Than 1,000,000 copies of the Geffen Records Long Playing Record Album "Double Fantasy." It is a beautiful display piece, in overall Very Good condition with some scuffs to the plexiglass and small dings to the distressed-silver wooden frame, which measures approximately 21" x 17".

**Beatles - John and Cynthia Lennon Owned Glass Vase From Kenwood, 1965.** John and Cynthia lived in the country home known as Kenwood from 1964 until 1968. Although their marriage ended in divorce, there were many happy times had there, and the Lennon estate was very near the home of Ringo and Maureen Starr known as Sunny Heights. The vase offered here was purchased by John and Cynthia while on holiday with the Starrs in 1965. It is Italian glass of flattened bottle form, orange and yellow cased in clear glass, 18" high. In overall Very Good condition with a small chip at the bottom. _Includes a handwritten COA from Cynthia Lennon which reads: "This ornament was bought by John and myself (along with another in the shape of a fish which has since been broken). We bought it on the holiday island of St. Vincent with Maureen & Ringo (Starr). It took pride of place in our bedroom at Kenwood. C. Lennon"_
Provenance: Christie's Pop and Guitars sale number 7322, London, 5 September 1996, Lot 443.
**Beatles - John Lennon****_Imagine_****Promo Store Display (1971**). A 12.25" square glossy album slick of the legendary Lennon album on white cardboard. The back has a fold-out easel and a pull-up hanging tab giving the record store a choice between hanging it or setting it on a shelf or counter. VG-EX 6.

**Beatles Related - A Bagism Performance Bag From Yoko Ono, circa late 1960s.** John and Yoko publicly introduced the concept of Bagism at a March 1969 press conference in Vienna, although they'd appeared in a bag performance piece in late 1968 at an artists gathering held at the Royal Albert Hall. Ono's background in performance art predated her involvement with Lennon - she'd been involved with the New York art scene since the early 1960s, and had received great attention for _Cut Piece_, which she debuted in 1964 and famously performed at Carnegie Hall in 1965. And while _Cut Piece_ hinged on the removal of the clothing which covers one's body, Bagism literally involved wearing a bag over one's entire body to shade the individual from any preconceptions based on race, gender, appearance, etc. By doing so, the idea was that "pure communication" could be achieved.
This very rare lot is a black cotton bag which came to it's original owner through Yoko Ono, likely in the late 1960s. The owner attended a party also attended by Ono and expressed interest in acquiring one of her bags for the purpose of meditation, which was later arranged and the bag delivered. It is in Excellent condition, sewn on three sides and without tags or labels, and measuring 67" x 51". _Includes a letter of provenance from the original owner who obtained the bag through Ono._
Provenance: Christie's Pop Memorabilia Sale 4388; London, 29 August 1991; Lot 556
**Beatles - Paul McCartney Signed Hofner Bass Guitar.** A B Bass Icon Series Hofner four string electric bass, strung left-handed and signed in 2007 on the pearloid pickguard in black marker. Excellent condition, with hardshell case. _LOAs from Perry Cox and Frank Caiazzo._

**Beatles - Paul McCartney Signed Color Tour Book Page.** An 8.75" x 11.75" color promo ad from the New World Tour book for the album _Off the Ground_ picturing the entire band and signed in silver felt tip by McCartney. The autograph was obtained on June 3, 2007, in New York City. Excellent. _COA From Heritage Auctions._
**Paul McCartney and Michael Jackson****_Say Say Say_****Signed 45 Record Sleeve (Columbia 38-04168, 1983).** This second single from the two superstars was released in October 1983, which was definitely a great year for Michael Jackson - in addition to singles from _Thriller,_ he chalked up his seventh #1 of the year with the release of this terrific duet. It also holds the distinction of being the release that put Paul McCartney atop the singles chart for the last time in the US. Produced by George Martin, and taken from Paul's _Pipes of Peace_ LP, this picture sleeve is signed boldly in blue marker by McCartney and black marker by Jackson. Condition: EX 7 (sleeve) / NM 8 (disc). _With PSA/DNA sticker affixed to the sleeve._
**Beatles - Paul McCartney Signed Book:****_Yesterday, The Beatles 1963-1965_****by Robert Freeman**. (New York: Holt Rinehart and Winston, 1983), first American edition, first printing, 10.25" x 9.25". The front cover of this glossy hard cover book features a color shot from the _Beatles for Sale_ session and is signed by McCartney in blue felt tip. Robert Freeman was the favorite photographer of the Beatles during the early days of their worldwide fame. He shot the cover photos for five of their UK Parlophone albums: _With the Beatles_, _Hard Day's Night_, _Beatles for Sale_, _Help!_, and _Rubber Soul_, as well as John Lennon's first two book covers. Very Good condition. _COA From Heritage Auctions._
**Paul McCartney Signed Baseball.** A Rawlings Official Major League Baseball with a bold "_Paul McCartney_" signature in blue felt tip on the sweet spot. Perfect for either Beatles or sports collectors. Excellent. _COA From Heritage Auctions._

**Beatles - Paul McCartney & Wings****_Band on the Run_****RIAA White Mat Gold Record Award (Apple SO-3415, 1973).** The last album McCartney issued on the Apple label and winner of the 1975 Grammy Award for "Best Pop Vocal Performance By a Duo, Group or Chorus." According to the plaque beneath the gold disc, this award was "Presented to Paul McCartney & Wings to Commemorate the Sale of More Than One Million Dollars Worth of the Apple Records Long-Playing Record Album 'Band On The Run'". Don't miss out on this one! Framed to an overall 17.5" x 21.5" and in Excellent condition.
**Beatles - Paul McCartney "Put It There" White Label Promo 45 Single (Capitol 7PRO-79074, 1989).** Brilliant copy of an ultra-rare promo. How rare? Noted Beatles expert Perry Cox estimates a mere 5-6 exist! The uncharted tune - on both sides of the disc - is from Sir Paul's _Flowers In The Dirt_ LP. Condition: MT 9 (original sleeve)/ MT 9 (disc).
**Beatles - Paul McCartney "Another Day" 10" One-sided Acetate (US - Apple, 1971)** Sir Paul's first solo single following the Beatles breakup was released on February 19, 1971. This acetate version was produced in very limited numbers, and this one's a nice copy. Condition: EX 7

**_Dylan in Woodstock_****by Elliot Landy Deluxe Limited Edition Book #75/100 (Genesis Publications, 2000).** This lavish book contains some of the most intimate photos of the oft-reclusive Bob Dylan ever seen. The 144 pages are filled with Elliot Landy's informal and atmospheric images of Bob Dylan, as he retreated from his first wave of worldwide fame, to live a quiet country life in 1966 with his new wife. Along the way, he reinvents himself musically with help from the Band. The book is as beautiful on the outside as the photos inside, with a supple brown suede binding, gilded page edging, and a slipcover. Included is an additional packet containing a color photo, signed by Landy. A rare book with some very minor handling wear; otherwise in Excellent condition.
**Bob Dylan****_Thin Wild Mercury: Touching Dylan's Edge_****Deluxe Limited Edition Book #85/1500 (Genesis Publications, 2006).** Jerry Schatzberg wrote this award-winning book covering several hundred photos of Dylan, taken by Schatzberg, many of which are previously unreleased, into 294 leather-bound pages, with silver edging, all housed in a cloth bound slipcase, with an extra art print signed by the author, and a cloth bag in which to store the book. All are in Excellent condition. The original shipping box is included.

**Eagles Autographed First Album,****_Eagles_****(Asylum SD-5054, 1972)** The Eagles' self-titled debut album laid the groundwork for what would become a very dominant strain of American popular music in the 1970s: melodic California based country-infused rock that was not too hard and not too soft. The album's lead track and first single, "Take It Easy," can be seen as a manifesto of the movement, and was listed as one of "The 500 Songs That Shaped Rock & Roll" by the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. This copy of the LP has been beautifully signed on the front cover by the original band members Don Henley, Joe Walsh (both in black marker), Glen Frey, Don Felder (both in blue marker), and Randy Meisner (in blue ink). The signatures have been dated to the 1990s. The LP has been matted for framing by the current owner, which is how it is being offered here. In Excellent condition. _COA from Perry Cox._

**Everly Brothers****_Terry Slater_****Stage Played Bass With Original Hardcase (Gibson, c. 1963).** A _circa_ 1963 Cherry Red Gibson EB3 bass, given by Chet Atkins (who originally purchased the bass) to Terry Slater, guitarist and/or bass player with such musical royalty as Little Richard, Jerry Lee Lewis, Duane Eddy, Bo Diddley, Muddy Waters, Chuck Berry, The Rolling Stones, Gene Vincent, Ray Charles, and more. Terry used this bass on every single recording that he ever did with the Everly Brothers. He also played the bass for Eric Burden (The Animals) and Glen Campbell, and as the story goes, they would all trade off instruments during their jam sessions, so this bass has been played by many famous people. When Terry stopped playing for the Everly's, he put the bass up, and it has been in storage ever since, until he graciously let us place it in this auction for you to bid on. The bass comes in its original case (one latch is missing), with normal wear for a touring bass case. The guitar is in very nice shape for a well used professional instrument. There are a few small dings and scratches on the neck and the body, some chrome loss from finger wear on the neck pickup, and oxidization on the bridge pickup; otherwise in Excellent condition. A true piece of Rock and Roll history!

**Carl Donnell "Kansas" Fields Passport Signed by Frank Sinatra Plus A Billie Holiday Handwritten Letter, 1950s.** "Kansas" Fields was a Jazz drummer, beginning in Chicago in the late 1920s; he played with Cab Calloway, Sidney Bechet, Dizzie Gillespie, Ella Fitzgerald, and more, and recorded with John Coltrane and Kenny Burrell in the 1950s.. Here's his passport from 1952, featuring numerous stamps from countries he visited plus his signature in three different places. Additional signatures of Frank Sinatra and Ava Gardner appear on page 8; and a Christmas card Billie Holiday sent to the drummer is included, handwritten in black ballpoint ink, reading in part"Hey Kansas / What's happening / with my trunk... / I've / got to have those / things. / Have a Merry Christmas / Lady Day."Also included is a small flyer from a French nightclub dated 1953 noting Frank Sinatra's name -- interestingly, the date on this flyer is the day that Sinatra, Gardner, Holiday and Fields met. Items are 4" x 9.5" and smaller; Very Good condition overall.
**Peter Frampton****_Frampton Comes Alive_****Platinum Record Award (A&M SP-3703, 1976).** A double-record set recorded live, this was the top-selling album for all of 1976 and one of the best sellers of all time with current worldwide sales of over eleven million. According to the plaque beneath the platinum disc on this in-house award, it was "Presented to Bob Scharbert For Helping Make the Peter Frampton Album 'Frampton Comes Alive' Sell Over a Million Copies by A & M Records". Scharbert was an employee of A&M Records. Framed to an overall 16" x 16" and in Excellent condition.

**Art Garfunkel****_Watermark_****RIAA Gold Record Award (Columbia JC 34975, 1977).** His third solo album which included the hit single "(What a) Wonderful World" where James Taylor and his former partner Paul Simon sang harmonies. According to the plaque beneath the gold disc, this award was "Presented to Columbia Records to Commemorate the Sale of More Than 500,000 Copies of the Columbia Records Long-Playing Record Album 'Watermark'". Framed to an overall 16.75" x 20.75" and in Excellent condition.
**Grateful Dead - Dennis Larkins Original Concept Artwork for Santa Fe Concert (c. 1983).** Three drawings, rendered in pencil on paper; the first depicts a skeleton dressed as a Kachina; the second a Navajo rug with text reading "Grateful Dead / Santa Fe;" and the third a skeleton cowboy riding a skeleton horse; all signed in pencil in the lower right corner by the artist. Artwork averages 10.5" x 10.5", matted and framed with glass for an overall size of 41" x 16". Excellent condition.
**_Grateful Dead_****_The Official Book of the Deadheads_****First Edition Signed by Ken Babbs, Ken Kesey, Stanley Mouse, and Paul Grushkin.****(William Morrow & Company, 1983).** Oversized, 209 pages, heavily illustrated, with dust jacket illustrated by Alton Kelley. Two of the large felt tip signatures on the half-title page are of Merry Pranksters- "_Grateful Babbs_" (Ken Babbs) and "_Dear Dredful Krazy_" (Ken Kesey), the other is of poster and LP cover designer Stanley Mouse where he includes a drawing of a mouse. The author/ editor Paul Grushkin has signed on the full-title page. According to the consignor, this copy came from the personal collection of renowned counterculture collector Richard Synchef. A book that no Deadhead should be without. Fine condition.

Source: https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/365761
Title: Edwin Austin Abbey - And none knew why he fed them both with his own hands, illustration to "Quince" - The Metropolitan Museum of Art
Chunks: 0,1,2,3
Abbey moved to England in 1878 to research illustrations to historical poems for Harper's and settled there permanently in 1883. This drawing is one of a series that responds to "Everyday Characters," poems by the British poet W. Mackworth Praed. We see the elderly bachelor Quince, a denizen of a West Country village, feeding his horse. The related stanza reads:
For full ten years his pointer Speed
Had couched beneath her master's table;
For twice ten years his old white steed
Had fattened in his master's stable;
Old Quince averred, upon his troth,
They were the ugliest beasts in Devon;
And none knew why he fed them both,
With his own hands, six days in seven.
Reproduced as a wood engraving, the image appeared in Harper's "New Montly Magazine," vol. 79 (June 1886), p. 29.
